observation.visible_scene: An indoor, slightly low-angle view of a window-mounted air-conditioning unit whose front cover is removed, exposing the grey metal evaporator coil and fin stack inside a painted metal frame; a boxy side housing sits at the left. A person's right hand, emerging from a black sleeve at the lower right, grips a black-and-yellow handheld spray/steam tool whose nozzle is pointed into the right side of the open coil, with a ribbed hose trailing downward. Behind the unit is a window with mullions, other buildings visible outside, and a loose electrical cable running along the ceiling.
visible_changes: The handheld nozzle is held close to the exposed coil and continuously emits a faint white vapor/mist around its tip, which drifts and thickens in several frames (most visible from mid-clip onward), indicating an ongoing spray/steam process rather than a single burst.

The hand and tool make small positional adjustments: the nozzle shifts slightly up, down, and across the right portion of the coil face, moving incrementally between frames while remaining aimed at the same general area.
The AC unit, its coil, the side housing, and the window frame stay fixed in place throughout; only the hand/tool and the mist change relative to them.

The overall camera framing drifts a little (the building edges outside and the ceiling cable shift position within the frame), consistent with minor handheld camera motion superimposed on the subject motion.
outside_clip_unknowns: What occurs before the first frame and after the last frame, including whether the cleaning/spraying starts or ends.
Whether the unit is powered or being serviced, and the full purpose or outcome of the procedure.
The exact fluid being emitted (steam, water, or cleaning solution) and the tool's mechanism, which are not directly visible.
uncertain_details: The precise identity of the tool (steam cleaner, pressure washer, or spray gun) cannot be confirmed from appearance alone.
The distinction between camera movement and hand movement is small; some apparent shifts of the nozzle relative to the coil may partly reflect camera drift.
Whether the visible haze is steam condensation, atomized liquid, or dust being dislodged is not determinable from the frames.
